# Goku remake plan (planning lane, 2026-10-10)

Branch `ws/goku-remake-plan`. This is a plan and a choosing sheet. **No fighter file was rewritten.** The owner picks each
animation by hand from [REMAKE-CANDIDATES.md](REMAKE-CANDIDATES.md) (one row per Melee slot, a recommended pick, a blank
"owner pick" column; same data as `remake-candidates.json`, regenerated by `tools/remake_sheet.py`).

Owner's brief: "go through and 'remake' him. No walking animations, assume he's always floating. Combos in the custom system can
move over as is, but this time we go through and deliberately choose each move's animation by hand. But we can plan better around
combos." Owner update the same day: "Just use the animations, we can author hitboxes after. I've noticed a lot of hitboxes that do
not make sense that were made/generated."

Decisions already in force and **not reopened here**: Marth mobility values (option c; the owner's uncommitted `gameplay.json` in
the main checkout was read, not touched), Kamehameha design (10 s charge, chant tiers, Mewtwo hold, Max 15 / Super 24), combos need
not be true and are percent-dependent, no combo brute forcing, no disc/XV2 data in git.

Contents: 0 What changes and what does not · 1 Hitbox policy (no generated hitboxes) · 2 Always-floating locomotion ·
3 The candidate sheet and how to preview · 4 Combo plan · 5 Phases and tests · 6 Audit of current generated hitboxes ·
7 Owner decisions.

## 0. What changes and what does not

| keeps | changes |
|---|---|
| model, 20-unit height, bone map (`ROLE-MAP.md`), toon, ECB-at-TopN fix, hurtboxes, landing-lag range check | **every ground locomotion row** is a floating clip (no walk/run/crouch from the ground-standing set), the hover is uniform (no "ANCHORED" rows) |
| Kamehameha, KiCharge, Instant Transmission, Counter/Riposte mechanics (scripts, Lua, articles) | each normal/aerial/grab/throw/getup/taunt row is chosen by the owner from the sheet |
| the 7-state combo package and 28 routes (carried over unchanged, section 4.1) | **all generated hitboxes are removed** from normals, aerials, grabs, throws and Rush/RushCombo/Riposte (section 1); the owner authors them in the Workbench |
| fidelity ledger discipline (zero silent placeholders) | the ledger gains an explicit hitbox axis (`HB-NONE` / `HB-AUTHORED`) |

## 1. Hitbox policy: no generated hitboxes

Owner: pick animations only; hitboxes are authored by hand afterwards. Section 6 lists the current generated ones that look wrong.

**Rule.** A remade move ships as *animation + timing only*. Its `moves/<name>.genoasm` keeps the waits, sound, gfx, IASA, movement
and landing-lag commands and carries **no `hitbox` command**. `gameplay.json` keeps `design` damage/angle/KBG/BKB as **proposed
numbers** (gameplay numbers are fine to commit per the standing policy) but no `radius`, `role` or `offset`.

**Ledger.** `tools/fidelity.py` grows one column, **HB**, with exactly three values and no fourth:

| HB value | meaning | allowed in a release? |
|---|---|---|
| `HB-NONE` | animation + timing present, no hitbox; has a **strike window** (frames) recorded as timing metadata only | no (move is inert) |
| `HB-AUTHORED` | hitbox authored by hand in the Workbench; carries author + date + the commit | yes |
| `HB-GENERATED` | produced by a tool/heuristic | **never in the remake**; the check fails |

The check (`tools/remake_check.py`, phase R0) fails the build if any move that is not `HB-NONE` lacks the authored stamp, and if any
`.genoasm` contains a hitbox command while the ledger says `HB-NONE`. That is the "zero silent placeholders" rule applied to hitboxes.

**Staying playable and testable while moves are inert.**

1. *Look/feel*: moves still play, cancel and land on their timing (IASA, autocancel, landing lag stay). The animation is checked in
   the Workbench / Blender (`launch_goku.py`) and the LAB CLIPS page (`ports/goku-xv2/tools/clips.ps1`), which is how the owner picks.
2. *Strike markers, not hitboxes*: each move records `strike: [first, last]` (the frames the owner sees the hit land). It is metadata:
   drawn as a marker on the Workbench timeline (queue item 7), used by the route-window check, never an in-game collider.
3. *Combos while inert*: `on: hit` routes cannot fire with no hits. Phase R3 validates them **statically**
   (`remake_check.py`: source and target exist, window inside the move, window opens at or after `strike[0]`, ki costs sum, no route
   shadowed) and visually with the Blender "play a string" tool, which chains moves at route windows (queue item 7, design approved).
   The first real hit-driven test happens per move as soon as the owner authors that move's hitbox: one smoke string per route
   (a handful of runs, not a sweep; no brute forcing).
4. *Specials that already own their hit logic* (Kamehameha beam, KiBlast, Counter window) are not "generated hitboxes" in this sense:
   the owner accepted the Kamehameha design. They stay, but are named in section 6 so the owner can say otherwise (decision D3).
5. *Not-yet-authored moves must not look finished*: LAB shows "HB-NONE" in the frame-data panel for the move; the release gate is
   "no HB-NONE move on the character-select roster" (Goku stays hidden / `work in progress` until his moves are authored).

## 2. Always-floating locomotion

### 2.1 What exists

The current build is a **hybrid hover** (owner, 2026-10-09): ground rows are baked so the lowest mesh point is held 2.0 model
units above the floor (`HOVER_Y`, `xv2_to_artist.py`), attacks/grabs/escapes/getups are **ANCHORED** (feet on the line at their
lowest frame, blended in and out over 6 frames), Wait is XV2's `GOK_BAS_STAND_S` (the "_S" = sky variant), and the ECB hip slot is
TopN so the ECB bottom is the root in every pose. Walk, Run, Squat and Landing still come from ground-standing XV2 clips
(`GOK_BAS_WALK`, `GOK_BAS_RUN`, `GOK_BAS_JUMP` crop). The physics is Melee's ground physics throughout; the lift is animation only.

XV2 has the right clips already: every "_S" clip is the in-sky version (`STAND_S`, `STEP_*_S`, `GRD_*_S`, `STUN_*_S`, `DMG_*_S`),
plus `BAS_BUKUU_{UP,DOWN,F_S,B_S,L_S,R_S}` (hover/fly in every direction) and `BAS_BOOST_F_{00,01,02}` (boost launch, sustained
boost, brake). `BUKUU` is the XV2 word for floating.

### 2.2 Options

| | option | how it stays a legal Melee fighter | cost | risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Visual hover, Melee ground states (recommended)**. Keep every ground state on Melee's ground physics and ECB, replace *all* ground clips with floating clips, lift the whole row set by one constant (`HOVER_Y`), drop ANCHORED/blend machinery | ground/ledge/platform/tech/shield/jump logic is the retail state machine, unchanged; nothing new for the engine, netplay or rollback | animation work only; deletes `ground_blend()` and the 6-frame ramps | hovering above the floor reads as "floating" but his hurtboxes sit 2 units higher: low attacks need the fatter feet hurtboxes already added; shadow stays on the floor (engine fix exists) |
| B | A + engine **`hover` on grounded states**: a per-define `ground_lift` (units, with a small bob) added to the root joint translation in grounded motions only, so the clips are authored at floor height and the lift is tunable at runtime | same as A, plus one engine value; hurtboxes/hitboxes follow because it moves the joint, not the draw | an engine edit in the game repo (needs `geno.md` update, schema key, rollback-safe because it is a constant of the define, not state) | engine lane, version bump, shared sources; the lift must be zero on ledge/down/capture rows by an explicit list |
| C | True levitation: Goku's "ground" is a `geno.air` state with locked Y and platform logic reimplemented | none of Melee's ground rules apply by themselves; platform drop-through, ledge snap, tech, wavedash, shield drop, landing detection all become hand-built | very high | breaks the "legal Melee fighter" brief; not recommended |
| D | A + lift the ECB by `HOVER_Y` so the collision capsule matches the body | physics matches the visual (no "I was hit on the floor" mismatch) | one `ftdata` ECB change | ECB bottom off the floor breaks ground detection assumptions (landing, tech, ledge); not recommended |

**Recommendation: A now, B as a later option.** A is exactly what the owner approved on 2026-10-09 (hybrid hover) pushed to its end:
the only difference in the remake is that *no row is a standing clip*. B is worth doing only if re-baking lifts into every clip proves
a maintenance burden (each rebuild already does it from one constant, so probably not). One extra thing A should add and does not
have today: a lower `traction` and slightly longer `walk`/`dash` deceleration so he *glides* instead of braking like a foot-planted
fighter; attribute values are the owner's decision (D2), the engine already reads them (46 importer attributes).

### 2.3 Row-by-row design (ground state machine kept; clip swapped)

| Melee row(s) | role | floating replacement (recommended; alternatives in the sheet) | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wait, Rebirth(Wait), Sleep | idle | `GOK_BAS_STAND_S` (kept) | Sleep currently still uses the ground `STAND`; switch |
| WalkSlow/Middle/Fast | walk | drift: `GOK_BAS_BUKUU_F_S` at three rates (40-frame loop) | there is no walk; "walk" is a slow float. Melee needs a loopable clip whose rate scales with stick |
| Run | run | `GOK_BAS_BOOST_F_01` loop crop (257 frames sustained boost) | currently `GOK_BAS_RUN` (ground run) |
| Dash, RunBrake, TurnRun | dash start, stop, run-turn | `BOOST_F_00` / `BOOST_F_02` (kept) / authored 180 over `BOOST_F_02` | `CMN_BAS_BRAKE_S` (55f) is an alternative brake |
| Turn | wait turn | `CMN_BAS_TURN` (27 frames) if it floats, else the authored yaw on Wait (kept) | needs the preview |
| Squat, SquatWait, SquatRv (crouch) | crouch | **descend / compress**: `GOK_BAS_BUKUU_DOWN` hold (a floating crouch is "sink and tuck"); no ground contact | ANCHORED today; becomes HOVER-low (dips 1.0 below idle but never touches) |
| KneeBend (jump squat) | jump start | `BUKUU_UP` first frames or `BOOST_F_00` first frames | Melee uses 4-frame squat (`jump_startup_time`) |
| JumpF/B, JumpAerialF/B | jumps | `BUKUU_UP` rise, `STEP_*_S` for air jumps, `JUMP_FRONT/BACK_*` as alternatives | the owner already called the current picks poor (punch list #9). Rows must be <= 40 frames (queue item 4) |
| Landing, LandingAir*, LandingFallSpecial | land | settle: `BOOST_F_02` tail or `STEP_F_S` end into Wait; no crouch | landing lag frames are Melee's; a floating settle is just a bob |
| Fall, FallAerial, FallSpecial, Pass | fall | `BUKUU_DOWN` loop | |
| Guard family | shield | `GOK_GRD_KAMAE_S`, `GRD_L_S` (kept, they are the _S variants) | already floats |
| Escape F/B/N/Air | dodges | `STEP_F_S`, `STEP_B_S`, `STEP_L_S` (kept); air dodge `STEP_*_S` | |
| Downs (Down*, Passive*) | on-the-floor states | `CMN_BAS_DOWN_*_S` (kept); he lies *just above* the floor (HOVER-low) | "always floating" taken literally: no row touches the floor |
| Ledge (CliffCatch, Wait, Climb, Attack, Escape) | ledge | hang by one hand with the body floating level: reuse `BUKUU_UP` last frame for the grab, `BUKUU_F_S` for climb; options in the sheet | the engine only needs the ledge-snap offset to match the pose; retail ledge states unchanged |
| Damage, tumble, DeadUp* | hit | `CMN_DMG_*` (and `_S` where it exists) | |
| Entry / victory / taunt | showpiece | `GOK_DEM_START`, `BAS_STAND_SS3`, `STAND_00_S/01_S` | |

### 2.4 Engine / Geno implications

* **Option A needs no engine feature.** Everything is in `xv2_to_artist.py` (a single `HOVER_Y`), `fighter.json` rows and
  `ground_modes.json` (currently empty).
* One thing to **verify** before rows are swapped (owed, needs a run): a floating clip changes which joints enter the ECB
  computation; the TopN-in-hip-slot fix removed that dependence, so landing from `BUKUU` aerials should not sink (gate:
  `lua/landing_check.lua`, 40 landings, 0 sinking).
* **Ledge**: the hang pose must put the hand where the ledge snap puts the root; the six ledge rows "hang below the ledge by design"
  today (ledger). The remake keeps that rule and verifies with `lua/ground_check.lua`.
* **Platforms**: drop-through and platform landing are retail; a hover of 2.0 means he stands 2.0 above the platform surface. Visible
  only on platform edges. Acceptable, it is the approved hybrid.
* **Tech/shield/airdodge/jumps**: retail rows with new clips; no logic change. Wavedash/airdodge into ground is retail behaviour; fine.
* Option B would add one schema key (`ground_lift`) and a version bump; flagged as a game-lane follow-up, not part of this plan.

## 3. The candidate sheet and how to preview

Files (all in this directory, committed): `REMAKE-CANDIDATES.md` (the sheet), `remake-candidates.json` (the data), `tools/remake_sheet.py`
(regenerates the sheet and, locally, an HTML sheet with embedded thumbnails), `tools/remake_preview.py` (Blender: renders a 6-frame
montage and metrics per clip).

Previews are **XV2-derived renders**, so they stay local and ignored: `_build/goku-xv2/remake-previews/<clip>.png` (6 frames from first to
last, character facing right, one fixed frame box per clip) and `_build/goku-xv2/remake-previews/metrics.json` (peak reach, peak
height, pelvis range/travel, fastest-limb frame per clip). `_build/goku-xv2/remake-previews/candidate-sheet.html` embeds them.

Ways to look at a candidate (every sheet row says which fits):

| how | command | shows |
|---|---|---|
| montage PNG (offline, no game) | open `_build/goku-xv2/remake-previews/<clip>.png` | 6 poses, forward = right |
| Blender (the Workbench's Goku scene) | `python tools/blender/geno_workbench/launch_goku.py` then select action `<clip>` on `GokuExport` (all `x*` clips are actions in `goku.blend`) | full scrub, any camera |
| LAB CLIPS page (in game, real model/toon) | `& 'ports\goku-xv2\tools\clips.ps1' <clip>` (e.g. `xGOK_ATC_007`) or console `lab clips play xGOK_ATC_007 12` | the clip in the game, pausable, speed x0.1 to x2 |
| XV2 move map | `_build/goku-xv2/movemap/index.html` (from `tools/movemap.py`) | which BAC/input uses the clip in XV2 and its timeline |

Selection criterion is **animation merit only** (readability of the pose silhouette, feel, startup/impact/recovery timing against the
Melee slot's role, direction, combo role). Hitbox shape fit is not used.

## 4. Combo plan

### 4.1 Carried over unchanged (28 routes, 7 states, 7 strings; `combo/combo.json`)

Light string `jab1 > jab2 > Light3 > Light4 > Light5` (L1..L5, windows from BAC cancel frames), heavy enders `HeavyRush` (forward,
from L1..L4), `HeavyFinish` (after L5), `HeavyUp` (launcher), `dsmash` (down), `Lx>Dragon Rush`, `Lx>Ki Volley`, `Launcher>Jump`
(`jump_short`), air string `Uair>Nair`, `Nair>Nair` (depth 2), `Nair>{fair,uair,dair}` enders, `Rush>RushCombo`. Ki meter 0-100: +4 hit,
+1.5 taken, KiCharge fills 0.8/frame, Counter costs 10, Super Kamehameha needs 100. These are untouched by the remake and are
re-validated statically (section 1, point 3). When a state's *clip* changes (`Light3` = `ATC_017`, `Light4` = `ATC_009`, `Light5` =
`ATC_022`, `HeavyRush` = `ATC_007`, `HeavyFinish` = `ATC_013`, `HeavyUp` = `ATC_004`, `KiVolley` = `ATC_027`) the route windows
are re-derived from the new `strike` frames, not from the old BAC windows; the sheet lists those combo-package states as slots too.

### 4.2 Proposed cleaner architecture (designed around the remade set)

Problems in the carried-over graph: five light states plus three heavy states all re-route into the same four enders (a 5 x 4
cross-product, 20 of the 28 routes), enders are chosen by stick direction at the press, every ender is available from every link so
the string has no decisions, `Lx>Rush` and `Lx>Ki Volley` are available at link 1 so nothing is earned, the air string is one
hard-coded sequence, and routes gate on `on: hit` only so they are unusable while hitboxes do not exist.

Proposal (all within the existing route system: `from` lists, `dir`, `priority`, `depth`, `once`, `ki_cost`, `when`):

| layer | moves | rule |
|---|---|---|
| Starters (ground) | jab1 (fast, safe), ftilt (spacing), dash attack, dtilt (low), utilt (anti-air) | any can begin a string (`starts: true`); jab1 is the only one that auto-chains by tapping A |
| Links (light, tap A on hit) | jab1 > jab2 > Light3 (3 links by default) | `Light4/5` become a **ki-gated extension**: `ki_cost 10` each, `depth 5`, so the long string is paid for |
| Branches (one stick direction each, from link 2 or 3 only) | forward: HeavyRush (knockback ender); up: HeavyUp (launcher); down: dsmash (low sweep) | one 3-source `from` list per direction instead of five, `priority` resolves overlaps; 20 routes become 6 |
| Cancels (special) | `Lx>Dragon Rush` costs 15 ki, `Lx>Ki Volley` costs 5 ki, both from link 2+ | specials become a *choice with a price*, not free |
| Air string | `Uair > Nair > Nair > {fair (ender) / dair (spike)}` after the launcher, the aerials the new animation set chose | enders keep `Nair>H` stick routes; `Launcher>Jump` `jump_short` stays |
| Route targets (what a route can enter) | `HeavyRush`, `HeavyFinish`, `HeavyUp`, `Light3/4/5`, `KiVolley`, `RushCombo`, `jump_short`, retail `dsmash/fair/uair/dair` | each target exists as a separate state only where it needs different timing than the retail move |
| Finishers | `HeavyFinish` (L5), `fair`, `dair`, Super Kamehameha (100 ki) | the three that cost a full string or the meter |
| Ki | earn +4 hit / +1.5 taken; spend: L4/L5 10 each, Rush 15, Volley 5, Counter 10, Super 100 | numbers are proposals, tunable in `combo.json` |

Net effect: 28 routes drop to about 18, each with a reason; no brute-force combo test is needed (owner decision of 2026-10-10: combos need
not be true). The proposal is a *design for the owner to approve* (D4); nothing in `combo.json` changes until then.

## 5. Phased implementation

| phase | what | gate (evidence) |
|---|---|---|
| R0 | tooling: `fidelity.py` HB column, `remake_check.py` (no-generated-hitbox gate, strike markers, route-window static check), `remake_sheet.py`; this plan | `remake_check.py` passes on the unchanged build (it should report every move HB-GENERATED, i.e. fail-as-expected), then passes after R2 |
| R1 | owner picks on the sheet (locomotion first, then attacks, grabs, getups, rest) | the filled "owner pick" column, committed as `remake-picks.json` |
| R2 | rebuild rows: `xv2_to_artist.py` row table from the picks, delete ANCHORED/`ground_blend()`, one `HOVER_Y`; strip hitbox commands from `moves/*.genoasm`, set `HB-NONE` + `strike` per move | `build.py` clean; ground audit "BELOW the floor: 0 rows" (`tools/ground_audit.py`), fidelity ledger "Placeholders a player can see: 0", `check_ir_integrity.py`, `tests/test_gameplay.py`, `test_ground_modes.py` |
| R3 | combo carry-over then redesign: carried routes validated statically, then the 4.2 graph if approved | `python -m tools.geno.combo combo.json`, `tools.geno check` (strings have routes), `combo/tests/route_table.py` static table |
| R4 | in-game checks, headless where possible, turbo (`MELEE_TURBO=1`) | `lua/ground_check.lua`, `ground_trace.lua`, `landing_check.lua` (0 sinking), `grab_check.lua` (26 cases x 4 victims), `pad_check.lua`, `second_match.lua`; **KAMECHECK** (`kame_check.lua`, unchanged behaviour: charge, store, roll, tiers, hold) because the swap of idle/jump/shield clips must not change the Kamehameha state flow; rewind: `gd.rewind_test` over 120 frames = **0 simulation bytes differ**; SyncTest rotation (`MELEE_SYNCTEST=12`) 0 mismatches |
| R5 | visual: strips (`lua/kame_strip.lua` style) for each locomotion row and every move with `lab clips`, the owner watches | **owed to a human with a monitor**; claims of look and feel are not "done" until the owner sees them |
| R6 | hitbox authoring by the owner in the Workbench hitbox panel (queue item 3), one move at a time; each authored move flips `HB-NONE` to `HB-AUTHORED` | per move: smoke string for its routes, then a LAB contact check on both facings |
| R7 | re-enable Goku on the roster | all moves `HB-AUTHORED`, ledger green, KAMECHECK + rewind 0 bytes + sync test |

Worker split suggestion (max 3 at once): one for the sheet/preview generation, one for the fidelity-ledger and checker code from the
specs in sections 1 and 5, one for the headless gate runs after R2. Reviewing and decisions stay with the lead.

## 6. Audit of the current generated hitboxes

Source: the built package `_build/goku-xv2/author-source/package/build/hitbox-positions.json` (native bank spheres evaluated through the
installed FigaTree; model Z = forward, Y = up, Goku about 16.6 tall, units model units), `gameplay.json`, `PARITY.md` "Move review",
`PUNCHLIST-2026-10-09.md`. "Frame" is the move's action frame. Every hitbox below was produced by `tools/attacks.py` / `cross_port.py` /
`gen_kame.py` rules (limb role + radius + window); none was authored by hand. The owner's observation ("a lot do not make sense") is
confirmed in principle: the shape and timing came from heuristics, never from watching the animation. This list is a checklist; the
*suspect* column is where the numbers themselves already look wrong. All entries are **to be removed in R2** and re-authored in R6.

| move | frames (active) | bone / size | measured position | why it looks wrong (suspect) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| jab1 | 3-4 | L hand r3.2 + L lower arm | Z 7.2..9.9 Y 12.3..12.7 | OK on the limb; but 2 spheres for a 2-frame punch, timing fixed by "strike f12 put on f3" (a retime) not the clip |
| jab2 | 4-5 | R hand r3.2 + R lower arm | Z 5.1..7.7 Y 9.4..12.5 | ledger: first window f6-9 was after the punch, moved to f4-5 by hand-measured peak; recheck against the picked clip |
| jab3 | 6-8 | L foot r3.8 + L shin | Z 3.5..7.2 Y 4.1..7.5 | kick sphere low (knee height) for a clip the owner has not reviewed |
| rapid_jab | 12-38 (5 x 3 frames) | R foot only r4.6 | Z 4.7..8.7 Y 2.8..6.4 | one right foot for the whole flurry although the clip alternates limbs; foot at ankle height |
| dash_attack | 8-14 | R foot r4.0 + R shin, 3 windows | Z -0.8..8.6 Y 8.3..9.7 | first frames at Z -0.8 (at the body, behind the foot) while the "flying side kick" has not extended yet: timing before extension |
| ftilt | 7-9 | R foot r3.8 + shin | Z 4.1..8.8 Y 10.9..11.4 | the tilt rows `AttackS3Hi`/`S3Lw` etc. are all the same clip (prototype reuse), so angled tilts hit identically |
| utilt | 8-12 | R hand r3.8 + forearm | Z -1.5..3.2 Y 12.3..18.7 | sphere travels from behind-the-body to above the head; the clip is the one the owner called "dumb" (punch list #2) |
| dtilt | 6-9 | R foot, shin, **root (`b_C_Base`)** | Z 4.2..8.4 Y 1.7..3.5 | the root sphere is a "floor-level" compensator for hovering, not a limb |
| fsmash | 12-15 | R hand r4.2 + forearm | Z 1.9..9.6 Y 3.1..13.8 | sweeps 10.7 high in 4 frames (low to head); `S4Hi/S4Lw` reuse the same clip |
| usmash | 12-16 | R hand r4.2 | Z 0.9..2.5 Y 16.4..18.9 | OK overhead; only 5 sampled frames; timing from the clip peak |
| dsmash | 8-11 | R foot, L hand, **2 root floor spheres** | Z -8.8..8.2 Y 1.4..2.8 | the two `FLOOR` spheres are not on limbs; the L hand at floor height is a guess for the "split sweep" |
| nair | 6-23 (18 frames, 3 windows) | both feet r3.8 | Z -5.8..8.6 Y 2.4..8.4 | an 18-frame active tail ("late" window f10-23) on a 40-frame row; spheres on both sides at once |
| fair | 10-12 | R foot + shin | Z 2.3..8.6 Y 8.9..10.3 | clip is the same split kick as nair (punch list #4: "effectively the same animation") |
| bair | 6-17 | R thigh + shin **r8.1** | Z -14.5..-3.9 Y 10.0..12.2 | radius 8.1 is huge (leg stretch scale-gain approximation of Luigi's bair); Luigi clip retargeted, hit spheres on UpLeg/Leg not on the foot |
| uair | 6-13 | L foot + shin r5.7 | Z -3.6..4.5 Y 10.9..18.7 | OK direction; radius 5.7 above hurtbox range |
| dair | 9-15 (owner's uncommitted edit; committed 6-8 and 9-14) | R foot r4.0 | Z -1.7..8.6 Y 8.2..10.1 | the foot is at hip height and **forward**, not below him, so it is not a stomp/spike (angle 270 spike from a forward kick); clip is the one the owner called grounded (#6) |
| grab / dash_grab | 8-15 | **root (`b_C_Base`)** r5.1 | fixed Z 9.3 Y 9.3 | a stationary sphere on the root, not following either hand; same for the pivot grab |
| pummel | 5 | R hand r4.6 | Z 6.2 Y 9.7 | single frame, unverified against the held pose |
| Rush (side B) | 9-16 | R hand r5.4 + forearm | Z -7.0..3.7 Y 13.2..14.4 | most of the active window the sphere is **behind or at the body** while the move dashes forward; `PARITY.md` says it was moved to the R foot at Z +8.4, but the built bank still reports the hand: ledger and build disagree |
| RushCombo | 6-24 | both hands, R foot r6.0 | Z -9.4..1.1 Y 2.5..12.1 | all spheres at or behind the body for a forward flurry; radius 6.0 |
| Riposte (counter kick) | 8-11 | R foot + shin r6.0 | Z -2.1..8.8 Y 4.5..11.3 | sphere starts behind him and is r6.0 (largest of the ground set) |
| ITEnd (Instant Transmission reappear) | 1-4 | **chest** r4.9 | Z 1.5 Y 10.6..11.8 | a body sphere that is a flinch hitbox, not a limb strike; the clip does not strike |
| Kamehameha beam, Super, Tap/Thin/Mid/Full/Max | per tier | beam article spheres | not in the file (article geometry is declared separately) | spheres chosen from `gen_kame.py` `TIERS`; the owner accepted the design, listed here for completeness (D3) |
| KiBlast, KiVolley | article | 2.2 radius sphere | not sampled | generated article; no limb |

Other recurring problems behind the list (from the ledger and `PARITY.md`): radii were set by a rule, not by looking at the animation;
windows were moved to match a retimed clip (the "strike f12 put on Melee f3" crops) so the animation frame the owner sees and the frame
the hitbox is live can differ; many rows reuse a single clip for several Melee slots (directional tilts, smashes), so a hitbox that is
correct for one is wrong for the other; and the root-attached "floor" spheres exist only to compensate the hover.
